themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Highest spike severity among all flagged issues this reporting period
reporting_angles: Are specific neighborhoods or corridors being targeted? Map the 3 complaints and interview residents.
Has DSNY enforcement staffing or posting-removal contractor changed recently?

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK versus 1.9 per week average over 8 weeks—a 220% increase (z-score: 3.54)—pointing to either increased street-level solicitation or resident frustration with existing encampments.
evidence: 6 panhandling complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average
Converges with encampment spike (20 complaints 2 weeks ago) suggesting homeless services gap
reporting_angles: Interview affected business owners and residents on high-traffic corridors (Broadway, St. Nicholas Ave) about recent changes.
Cross-reference with HRA/DSS homeless outreach data—are services keeping pace with visible encampments?

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints reached 4 THIS WEEK versus 1.0 per week average over 8 weeks—a 300% spike (z-score: 3.46)—suggesting potential public health or sanitation contractor responsiveness issues.
evidence: 4 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with broader sanitation surge (Illegal Posting, Curb Condition, Encampment all up this/last week)
reporting_angles: Identify specific locations of the 4 complaints—is there a contamination or rodent control issue in a particular area?
Has DSNY or Department of Health response time degraded? Check service request closure data.

themes_detail.label: Encampment Growth Sustained
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints hit 20 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 4.4 per week average over 8 weeks—a 357% spike (z-score: 4.07)—reflecting a sustained homelessness crisis in the district despite city initiatives.
evidence: 20 encampment complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 4.4 weekly baseline (357% increase)
Correlates with panhandling and dead animal spikes this week, suggesting cascading service gaps
Community board has repeatedly requested park safety staff and security enhancements (unfunded priorities)
reporting_angles: Profile specific encampment locations (parks, Under the Viaduct at Inwood, etc.) and interview unhoused residents about access to services.
Investigate whether city's street outreach teams have capacity for Washington Heights; compare with other high-need districts.
Connect to 2026 Inwood fire safety article—are unhoused residents living in unsafe conditions?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 0.2 per week average—a 1,100% increase (z-score: 6.35)—indicating either a bike-share system issue or enforcement lag in removing junk bikes from streets.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% increase)
May reflect Citi Bike expansion, theft recovery lag, or community board's unfunded litter/curb condition requests
reporting_angles: Did Citi Bike or another bike-share operator launch service in Washington Heights in recent weeks? Check expansion timeline.
Interview Parks Enforcement or Sanitation about removal procedures for abandoned bikes; compare closure times to other districts.
